lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's fit slurm.conf on one screen.
What tells Slurm which nodes your cluster has, and where its controller runs?
A text file, slurm.conf. A handful of its lines define the whole cluster, and you can learn to spot them at any site.
SlurmctldHost names the host where the controller runs.
NodeName lines describe the compute nodes, with their CPUs and memory.
PartitionName lines group nodes into partitions, the queues that jobs are submitted to.
And an include line pulls in another file, as if its lines stood right there.
sind splits these lines over two files. slurm.conf holds the cluster-wide settings, and ends with an include.
The included file, sind nodes dot conf, has a NodeName line for each worker sind manages, and the partition all.
sind rewrites it when you add or remove workers, and leaves slurm.conf as it was created.
Your own slurm.conf lines, from the main section of the cluster config, go just before that include.
So: a controller line, node and partition lines, and includes to split them up.
Next up: episode six, Rehearse a change. See you there!
